Settings & Sync

The surface whose whole job is trustworthiness — so every sentence on it has to survive being true
DRAWS    wireframes §12.1 – §12.7
READS    spec §C8 · §H1 · D-052 · D-054
STATUS   no Settings surface exists in the build
DATE     2026-07-29

One discriminator runs this whole sheet

Not "is sync on" — has this device ever synced. The privacy card and the erase dialog both key on it, and both would print a false promise if they keyed on the toggle. Turning sync off is a pause: nothing already sent is clawed back, the founding passkey outlives it, and the account still exists.

Which is why there are three states, not two

The middle one — synced before, sync now off — is the state a real user reaches every single time they pause sync, and it is the one a two-state design gets wrong. A card that said "no account, cloud sync or analytics" to a device that has an account would break the sentences §H1 calls product law.

Nothing here is a second tall layer

Settings is one task sheet with its own internal push stack. Currency, notifications, sync, import and privacy push inside it, back-only, swipe-to-close disabled while pushed. Units and Appearance are fitted picks, so they fit and close in place.

§12.1 · SETTINGS · NEVER SYNCED
THE PRIVACY CARD · ALL THREE STATES
Your data never leaves this device. No account, cloud sync or analytics. Export any time.
Privacy ›
Never synced — the default. §C8 verbatim, and the only state where "never leaves this device" and "no account" are honest.
No ads, trackers or analytics. Export any time.
This device syncs to your own server, so your other devices see the same records. It never leaves servers you run.
Privacy ›
Syncing. spec-delta's own wording, unchanged — it says where data goes and deliberately claims nothing more.
No ads, trackers or analytics. Export any time.
Sync is paused. Records you already sent are still on your server.
Privacy ›
Paused. Drops both claims that stop being true the moment an account exists, and states the fact instead. The card never re-earns those two sentences — not by turning sync off, not ever.

One line never leaves

D-006's floor — no ads, no trackers, no analytics, free complete export, sync strictly opt-in — is true in all three states, so it gets its own line and survives every switch. This changes what the build ships today: the current card drops the whole claim the moment sync comes on, which lets a user infer analytics might now exist.

Nothing on this card is the privacy page

Privacy › pushes a release-gated page this pass does not write. That page carries obligations the card must not pre-empt: drop the no-account claim, state that an operator can read server-side data, disclose Safari ITP. The card claims nothing that would contradict it.

Review notes is the second door

It shows a count when the queue has open items and None waiting when it does not, and it pushes the same queue page Home pushes. This is what keeps resolved items reachable after Home has stopped rendering the entrance — a decision is part of the record, not a deletion.

Appearance ships with the palette, not before

A Dark option that selects a palette nobody drew is worse than no control. Sheet 01 is what unblocks this row — and it deliberately does not take the inversion-pass shortcut that would be the tempting fix.

A version row, because there is no telemetry

With no analytics and no crash reporting, the user is the only channel. Giving them the build number is the cheapest possible support tool and costs nothing the privacy card claims.

02 · Sync — three states, pushed inside the sheet

Called Sync, not "Sync & devices" — there is no device registry, and a title promising a list Koi cannot produce is the wrong thing to put on the trust surface.

§12.3 · PAUSED
Never re-explains Face ID. This device already has a working passkey, so turning sync back on is a plain sign-in — one prompt. The two-prompt sentence belongs only to the never-synced state.

Turning off needs no confirmation

Neither direction does — enabling costs nothing undoable, and disabling only pauses future uploads. The toast reads Sync paused. Records already sent stay on the server. and the page it leaves behind is the paused state, not the never-synced one.

Failure has no badge, and that is on purpose

Not syncing: your server didn't answer. Your records are safe on this device. A sentence, not a raw error string — and no badge anywhere in the shell.

The consequence is recorded rather than smuggled around: a user whose sync has been broken for days finds out on a visit here. A dot on every root would nag from four places about something the car does not need from them.

One sentence covers both outcomes

A local-only device makes zero network calls, so it cannot know whether it is about to register the founding passkey or sign in with one that exists elsewhere. The copy promises neither and states the one fact that is always true.

Proven server-side only (D-054). Drawn so the shape is agreed, marked so nobody mistakes it for something that ships with this batch.

This device has no passkey for your account, and Koi has no way to enter a recovery code yet.

A real dead end, stated plainly rather than absorbed into "just tap again".

Amounts you logged never change.
Every row shows the user's own latest number converted. With a multi-car garage the number is the newest in the whole garage, shown with no car name — it is a format demonstration, not a fact about a car.
Volume is a fourth group, easy to forget because it never carries its own headline card — but it relabels the fuel keypad's LITRES pill, the Fuel lens footer, and every €/L on the app. With early data and nothing to convert, rows show the unit name alone — a made-up example is exactly the invented number the honesty rules forbid.
§12.7 · ERASE — THE ONE SPECCED LABEL THIS PASS CHANGES
Erase everything?
This deletes every car, record, reminder and document on this device. There is no undo.
Type ERASE to confirm
Cancel Erase
NEVER SYNCED
Erase this device?
Sync is turned off first, so your server can't send the records back.
This deletes everything on this device. Records already on your server stay there.
Type ERASE to confirm
Cancel Erase
HAS EVER SYNCED — SYNCING OR PAUSED
Once an account exists, a local wipe is not an erase. The device is still enrolled, so it re-bootstraps from the checkpoint and the records come straight back — erase-everywhere is explicitly not built.
So the act turns sync off first and says so, and the label becomes Erase this device for any device that has ever synced. A mislabelled destructive button is the worst possible place to promise something Koi cannot keep. Typed ERASE and There is no undo. are §C8 verbatim in both.
